This ignores the specific constraints of the problem (one box has 6 more coins than another) and the rules of the game (guessing less than the actual number yields a payout equal to the guess, while guessing higher yields nothing). By blindly guessing the minimum value for every box, Bob is likely to drastically underestimate the number of coins in the larger boxes, missing out on potential winnings. The optimal strategy requires analyzing the specific valid distributions derived in previous steps to find the guesses that maximize the minimum guaranteed return for *each* distribution, rather than applying a generic "guess the minimum" rule to all three boxes simultaneously. This error will lead to an incorrect calculation of the minimum guaranteed winnings.
